PORTED (lane gap-signin): the nine side-package tests and one new guard test now live in Tests/Unit/SignInStubTests.swift (proof 3): everyStubbedSignInRouteAsksOnlyAddressesOnThisMac (:119), microsoftSignInSendsPKCEAndStoresTheTokenOnlyInTheVault (:133), anAdminBlockedRedirectShowsTheLineTellingTheOwnerWhatToAsk (:158), anAdminBlockedTokenAnswerShowsTheSameLine (:174), otherRefusalsKeepTheProvidersOwnWords (:185), fastmailUsesAuthorizationCodeWithPKCEAndJMAPScopes (:194), theGoogleRouteIsUnreachableWhileTheVerificationFlagIsFalse (:207), signInWithChatGPTStoresAProviderCredentialAndTheNoteIsFixed (:223), aRedirectWithAnotherStateIsIgnored (:233), aRouteWithoutAnAppRegistrationSaysSo (:241). Loopback only: each stub listens on 127.0.0.1, every endpoint given to the service is a 127.0.0.1 address and the service is built with a reaches rule that refuses any other host (SignInStubTests.swift, signInOnThisMacOnly); a token is a stub string held in a MemoryVault and never printed. The app's SignInFlags.gmailAPIVerified is still a separate Bool that nothing sets from the Rust core (Sources/Features/SignIn/SignInController.swift, `public var flags`): the app test proves the engine flag, the Rust test (proof 2) proves the core flag; wiring the one source needs Sources/CoreBridge, outside this lane's files. The token lands in the vault seam: in the app it is KeychainVault (interim, Sources/Features/SignIn/KeychainVault.swift:5-8), in the tests a MemoryVault; core-secrets is not called (FFI has no StoreSecret). Proof 0 (the side package) is kept as the earlier run of the same nine tests.
